title: The Craziest Rocks In The World

title_pattern.template: The Craziest [everyday category] In The World
devices: superlative ('Craziest') applied to a boring everyday noun (rocks) = expectation violation
listicle promise without a number: implies a ranked tour
short, 6 words, no caps shouting, no colon
broad topic = broad audience; the channel brand (cute dog) carries the click more than the title
title_pattern.notes: Control video: performs at channel median (~5.7M), so this is the channel's baseline formula: 'boring thing X is secretly amazing' compilation of 5 sub-topics, each a mini-mystery with a mechanism explanation. Title is generic; the thumbnail does the specific promising.

thumbnail.composition: Pure white background, three subjects in a left-to-right row: glowing crystal fan rising behind the mascot dog's head (left), a tan rock with chrome cubes embedded (centre, largest), a smiling lumpy rock with a baby rock in a diaper on a green glow (right). Each has a short lowercase label above with a hand-drawn red curved arrow pointing down at it.
thumbnail.text: 'glows' / 'perfect cubes' / 'reproduces' in bold rounded black sans, lowercase, ~1/10 frame height each
thumbnail.colours: White field, black line-art, saturated rainbow neon glows (blue, green, yellow, red, cyan) top-left, metallic grey cubes, tan rocks, mint-green glow, single red accent repeated (dog collar + all three arrows)
thumbnail.subject_scale_contrast: No real scale gag; contrast is ordinary (brown rock) vs impossible properties (chrome cubes, rainbow glow, a baby rock). The mascot's cute face anchors the left third as brand recognition.
thumbnail.why_it_works: Three verbs-as-labels sell three separate 'that can't be true' claims at once (glows, perfect cubes, reproduces); the third is the most absurd and is the end-of-video payoff, so curiosity spans the whole runtime. White + one red accent reads instantly at small size and is consistent with the channel's brand, so returning viewers recognise it. Labels-with-arrows format is a cheap, repeatable template.

hook.verbatim_0_5s: I was in the museum the other day looking at all these cool rock formations on display.
hook.verbatim_0_12s: I was in the museum the other day looking at all these cool rock formations on display. You know, there were spiky rocks and goopy rocks, but when I made it all the way to the bottom, what I saw didn't make any sense.
hook.device: first-person anecdote cold open ('the other day') with mascot in a recognisable place, building to an open loop ('what I saw didn't make any sense') at ~11s; the reveal (rock with machined metal cubes) lands at 13-17s, then the host voices the viewer's skepticism ('am I dumb?'). No intro, no channel branding, no list preview in the audio; the thumbnail already promised the list.
hook.visual: Museum exterior wide -> gallery wide -> dog close-up with question marks; first visual change within 2s, 6 distinct frames in the first 12s.

beats.summary: First-person museum visit; walks past spiky and goopy rocks; something at the bottom 'didn't make any sense'.
A rock with perfectly machined metallic cubes fused into it, supposedly natural; host doubts it ('am I dumb?').
It wasn't fake; 'What sorcery is this?' transitions to section 1.
IMPOSSIBLY PERFECT SHAPED ROCKS: pyrite is a crystal, pulled as perfect cubes from a mine in Spain.
How it forms: iron and sulfur ions in hot water, crystallize as fluid cools; lattice and unit cell; pyrite unit cell is a cube.
Simplify to cube-shaped LEGO bricks stacking layer by layer -> fake-looking cube; intergrown clusters.
Cubic unit cell doesn't guarantee a cubic crystal (garnet dodecahedrons); table salt is cubic too.
Dog shelves the rock, accuses Earth of hiding more -> section 2 title.
MUSICAL ROCKS: ringing rock fields ring like bells; ancient lithophones.
1960s informal study: ringing rock expands after cutting -> internal stresses; more stress = higher pitch (joke: stress the rock out).
People stole the small ones and chip souvenirs from boulders, which permanently kills the ringing; 'take care of the earth'.
Earth tied to chair; UV flash; section 3 GLOWING ROCKS.
UV excites electron in activator atom, it falls back and emits a photon; billions at once = glow.
Fluorescence (spelling joke); activator element sets colour: manganese red calcite, uranium green autunite, molybdenum blue scheelite.
Phosphorescence: electron stuck via 'forbidden transition' (quantum rules), slow release; glow-in-the-dark stickers; recharge with black light.
'It doesn't stop here': thermo-, tribo- (sugar cube flash), electro-, radio-luminescence, each misspelled on screen.
'Rocks can form perfect shapes, sing, glow... what else?' -> MAGNETIC ROCKS.
Imagine early humans seeing lightning, fire, magnetic rocks ('witchcraft'); ancient belief rocks had a soul.
Magnetite normally only gets attracted; rarely it is a permanent magnet doing the attracting.
Earth's field too weak; theory: lightning strike magnetizes it -> lodestone, rare and near surface; NASA lab experiment reproduced it.
'Next you'll tell me some rocks are alive' -> LIVING ROCKS... MAYBE.
Trovants near Costesti, Romania; 'growing stone'; grow after rain; called dragon eggs; cut open -> tree-ring layers.
Porous rock absorbs minerals from rain, pressure expands it; ~4 cm per 1000 years; rain = feeding time.
They bud: a bulb breaks off as a baby trovant that also grows; pet-rock joke reversed to 'leave them in Romania'.
Host admits he didn't know much about rocks; soft like/subscribe; shelf of all rocks; fan-art end screen.

pacing.speech_density_note: Near-continuous VO with short comic pauses (0.5-2 s) for sight gags; deliberately casual delivery.
pacing.re_hook_interval_s: ~90-100 s: each new section opens with a title card + one-line 'impossible' claim; sub-hooks every 20-30 s ('but there's some debate', 'and it gets even worse', 'but it doesn't end there').
pacing.notes: Cut rate peaks in the glowing-rocks rapid list (24 hard cuts in 6:00-7:00). Shots are short but the frame is sparse: one idea per frame on white.

techniques_worth_copying: Mascot narrator as the viewer's proxy: reacts with skepticism ('am I dumb?', 'you're not fooling me') before the explanation, legitimising the viewer's disbelief.

Frame device: a museum trip + a recurring 'collection shelf' the mascot fills after each section; it acts as a progress bar and a callback that ties a listicle into one story; final shot shows the full shelf.
Recurring personified Earth character (sweating, tied to a chair, dragged by a magnet) as the transition gag between sections.
Section title cards in hand-drawn caps with a self-deprecating tiny subtitle; one card per section, 1.5-3 s.
Personify the abstract: atoms/electrons as cute characters that sweat, strain and get 'chained' (forbidden transition); stressed rocks with angry faces = higher pitch.
Concrete analogy ladder: lattice of tiny mascots -> unit cell highlight box -> LEGO brick -> brick stacking into a cube -> real pyrite photo.
Palette flip as a reveal: white world switches to dark navy for the glowing section, mascot turns neon mint; lights-on/lights-off toggles mirror the science (fluorescence vs phosphorescence).
Misspelled-word running gag for jargon (PHOSPHORESHENSH, RADIOLUMINESFFGTTHH): makes hard terms memorable and funny, escalates each time.

Escalation connectors before each next fact: 'And it doesn't stop here', 'But it doesn't end there', 'And it gets even worse'; recap of all prior wonders before the next title ('they can sing, they can glow, what else?').
Order sections by absurdity, ending on the most unbelievable (rocks that 'reproduce') which the thumbnail already promised.
Real photos used sparingly as proof: background-removed cut-outs with bold sans label + grey location subtitle, never full-bleed footage.
Single red accent (collar, arrows) across a white/black-line world keeps brand recognition and guides the eye.
Short, soft outro: honest 'I didn't know much about rocks' + fan-art end screen (community loop) instead of a hard sell.

code_only_remake_needs.feasibility: Very high. The style is flat 2D vector on white: thick black outlines, flat fills, minimal shading, sparse frames. Almost everything maps to SVG components in Remotion; only the ~15 real photos need replacing with SVG illustrations or licensed/own photos.
assets: Original mascot character (not a dog copy): SVG rig with head, body, arms, ~8 swappable expressions (neutral, squint, wide-eyed, worried, proud, angry-red), 4-6 arm poses, plus a 'glow' variant for dark scenes
Stick-figure extras (visitors, caveman, scientist with curly hair + glasses) as simple SVG
Personified prop characters: Earth with face, rock with face (calm/angry/crying), electron character, trovant blob with eyes
Collection-shelf scene component that accumulates items across sections
Title-card component: hand-drawn display font (e.g. a free marker-style font), tiny subtitle, row of icon decorations
Label component: bold sans caps label + small grey subtitle under an object

Diagram kit: orbit rings + nucleus + electron sprite with energy-level arrows; lattice grid generator with highlight box; ball-and-stick unit cell; field lines (bar magnet, Earth dipole); cross-section with stripes/rings; rain particles; '+ MINERAL' particles
Glow filter (SVG feGaussianBlur) and dark-palette theme toggle
motion: Mostly hard cuts with static holds; motion comes from pose/expression swaps every 1-2 s (two-frame 'boil' optional)
Pop-in with overshoot spring for labels and objects
Scale-up builds (brick multiplying into a cube, rock swelling)
Shake/jitter for shock, electrocution, angry rocks
Flash-to-white/grey for lightning and UV light; palette inversion transition
Line draw-on for field lines and arrows (strokeDashoffset)
Magnifier zoom: circular mask that scales up to fill the frame
code_only_remake_needs.audio: Casual first-person VO at ~160 wpm (Kokoro/Piper), comedic pauses for gags, light SFX (pop, bonk, zap, ring, hammer clink), soft background music; captions optional (original has none burned in)
code_only_remake_needs.effort_notes: 10-min episode = ~140 hard cuts / ~390 visual states. With a reusable character rig, prop library, and storyboard JSON driving shot templates (title_card, character+object, label_photo_substitute, diagram, gag_closeup, shelf_callback), this is tractable. The jokes and expressions carry retention more than the art, so the script must include explicit gag/expression cues per line.
